Seminar Title:

Optimizing Iron Loading in Hydroponic Amaranthus Microgreens: A Comparative Study of Chemical and Nano-Foliar Delivery Systems

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Biotechnology and Medical Engineering

Speaker Name:

Dibyabharati Panda

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

BM Seminar Hall (BM-140)

Date and Time:

10 Nov 2026 10:00 AM

Contact:

Dr. Prasoon Kumar

Abstract:

Iron Deficiency Anaemia remains a severe public health challenge in India, affecting over 50% of vulnerable demographics despite ongoing national interventions. Hydroponic microgreens offer a controlled, high-yield system to address this via agronomic biofortification, yet the comparative efficacy of different iron delivery agents remains understudied. This study evaluated the biofortification efficiency and the physiological impacts of three distinct iron sources applied as foliar sprays to Amaranthus microgreens. Microgreens were cultivated in a hydroponic system and treated with three iron formulations: Ferrous Sulfate (FeSO4), Iron chelate (Fe-EDTA), and Iron Nanoparticles (Fe-NPs) at three concentrations (5, 10, and 15 mg/L) in separate batches in triplicate. The treatments increased the physiological parameters and antioxidant efficacy in a concentration-dependent manner. ICP-OES analysis revealed iron accumulation increased progressively with increasing Fe-chelate and FeNP treatments up to 0.4145mg/g, whereas FeSO₄ showed a non-linear response, with the highest Fe accumulation (0.8565mg/g) observed at the lowest FeSO₄ treatment.
